author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1850
summary: 드물게 사는 텃새로, 울릉도를 비롯해 서해안과 남해안 섬의 바위 절벽에서 번식한다. 섬이나 해안의 암초와 암벽에 무리 지어 번식하며, 바위 절벽의 층진 오목한 자리에 마른 풀이나 해초로 접시 모양 둥지를 짓고 한배에 알 4~5개를 낳는다. 잠수하고 나면 바위에 올라 날개를 펴고 햇볕에 말린다. 국외에서는 러시아 극동과 사할린에서 일본 규슈 북부, 중국 황해 지역에 걸쳐 군데군데 번식한다.

art.subject: Japanese Cormorant (Phalacrocorax capillatus), adult outside the breeding season, as seen on Korean island coasts in autumn and winter: head, neck and underparts black with a green gloss; mantle, scapulars and wing coverts dark bronzy-green with neat black feather edges giving a scaly look; a small, narrow patch of bare yellow skin at the bill base, pointed behind the gape; a broad white cheek and throat patch below and behind the eye, its border angular and extending up behind the yellow skin; tail black. Bill long, grey-black with a hooked tip; iris emerald green; legs and webbed feet black.
art.pose: standing on a sea rock with wings spread to dry in the sun
art.scene: Korean offshore island in autumn or winter: steep layered rock cliffs and dark reefs above a grey sea; no people, buildings or text
views: adult non-breeding, side view perched on a rock: narrow yellow bill-base skin, broad white cheek patch with an angular border, green-glossed black body, scaly bronzy-green back and wing coverts, short tail
adult, front view standing on a rock with wings spread to dry: black wings held open, green-glossed black body, white cheek and throat
adult, flight side view: long neck outstretched, wings set slightly behind the middle of the body, short tail, straight body line
adult breeding (late winter to spring), side view perched: fine white plumes on the head and neck and a white patch on the thigh
art.build: Large, heavy seabird, about 84cm, with a long body, long thick neck and flat-crowned head. Bill straight, about as long as the head, ending in a sharp hook. Legs short, black, set far back, with fully webbed feet; stands upright on rocks. At rest the wings reach the base of the tail. Tail short and stiff. Swims low with the bill tilted up and dives for fish; perches with wings spread to dry. In flight neck outstretched, with the wings set slightly behind the middle of the body.
avoid: Do not paint a large yellow face patch with a rounded border reaching the eye; that is Great Cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo).
Do not paint bronze-brown upperparts; the back and wing coverts are distinctly greenish.
Do not give it a long tail or a duck-like bill; the bill is hooked and the tail short.
Do not show the white thigh patch or white head plumes on autumn and winter birds.
